newsitem.title: CHINA: Key 1997 dates in post-Deng China.
newsitem.headline: Key 1997 dates in post-Deng China.

text.p: Important events on China's political and diplomatic calendar for the rest of 1997 following the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping include:
February 24-25: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright visits China as part of her first world tour in her new post. The visit has been shortened because of Deng's death.

February 25: Funeral for Deng in Beijing's Great Hall of the People. The 459-member funeral committee is headed by Deng's anointed successor, Jiang Zemin. The funeral will not include a lying in state, and no foreign dignitaries have been invited.

March 1: The annual session of the National People's Congress, China's parliament, is expected to approve plans to roll back parts of Hong Kong's democracy and laws on civil liberties when the territory is handed back to China.
End March: U.S. Vice President Al Gore is expected to visit China to pave the way for an exchange of visits by President Bill Clinton and Chinese President Jiang Zemin.
July 1: Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule after more than 150 years as a British colony.

Expected in October: The Communist Party of China holds its 15th Congress, which is due to approve the country's political agenda into the 21st century. The congress will hold elections for the Central Committee, the Politburo and the Party leader.
